settings.title: What Scent Families Are
settings.body: A scent family groups fragrances by their dominant notes and character, woody, fresh, floral, sweet or spicy. Knowing the families turns fragrance from guesswork into a simple map you can navigate with confidence.
settings.tags: Oud & Woody, Fresh, Floral, Sweet, Spicy

settings.title: Find Your Family
settings.body: Think about the smells you naturally enjoy. Love warmth and depth? Try oud and woody or spicy oriental. Prefer bright and clean? Explore fresh and citrus. Drawn to flowers or dessert notes? Floral or gourmand await.

settings.title: Families & Longevity
settings.body: Character affects staying power. Rich oud, woody and oriental families tend to last longest, while fresh and citrus scents are lighter and brighter. Knowing this helps you match a family to the wear you want.

settings.title: Build Around What You Love
settings.body: Most people gravitate to two or three families. Once you know yours, you can build a scent wardrobe with confidence and branch into related families to discover something new but familiar.

settings.question: What are the different fragrance families?
settings.answer: The main fragrance families are woody, fresh, floral, and oriental, with gourmand and spicy often treated separately. We organise scents into five: Oud & Woody, Fresh & Citrus, Floral & Rose, Sweet & Gourmand, and Spicy & Oriental.

settings.question: How do I know my perfume scent family?
settings.answer: Notice the character you enjoy most. Warm and deep points to woody or oriental, bright and clean to fresh, flowery to floral, sweet to gourmand. Favourites usually cluster together.

settings.question: What is a woody fragrance?
settings.answer: A woody fragrance is built on warm wood notes like sandalwood, cedar and vetiver, often crowned by oud. These scents feel warm, deep and sophisticated, and last well.

settings.question: Which fragrance family lasts longest?
settings.answer: Rich families last longest. Oud, woody and oriental scents have heavy base notes that evaporate slowly, so they outlast lighter families. Fresh and citrus scents are brighter but fade sooner.

settings.question: How do I choose a perfume by scent family?
settings.answer: Start with the notes you already love, then explore that family. If you enjoy warmth, try woody or oriental; if you prefer freshness, explore fresh or citrus.
